readerTitle: Two businesses, same growth: what happens when the ads stop?
caseNote: 가상 사례 (B2B 회계 대행사, 주방용품 소매점, 미용실 예약 앱) · 모든 수치는 설명용
insight: 성장률이 아니라 성장의 출처를 본다. 광고비를 멈춘 달에도 손님이 계속 오는지가 성장의 질을 보여준다.
misconception: 성장은 성장일 뿐이다. 같은 40% 성장이면 어디서 왔든 가치가 같고, 자연 유입은 공짜다.

sources.text: 마케팅의 표준 개념 (유료 유입과 자연 유입의 구분)

factChecks.note: 차트 수치는 모두 설명용 가상 수치입니다. 광고 중단 3개월 동안 평소 대비 신규 고객 비율: 회계 대행사 95%·90%·93%, 주방용품점 35%·25%·22%. 3개월째 22%는 평소 대비 78% 감소이므로 본문에는 "about three-quarters"로 적었습니다.
두 사업의 "40% 성장"과 "같은 이익"은 비교를 위한 가정입니다. 실제 기업이나 연구를 인용하지 않았습니다.
검색 순위나 마켓플레이스 알고리즘 변경으로 자연 유입이 줄 수 있다는 내용은 일반적 서술입니다. 특정 사건이나 수치를 언급하지 않았습니다.

cards.title: Two businesses, same growth: what happens when the ads stop?
body: A bookkeeping firm and a kitchenware shop both grew revenue 40% last year. On paper, they look equally healthy.
Then both owners paused their marketing for three months. One barely noticed. The other almost stopped getting new customers.

image.label: Two shopfronts side by side, one busy, one quiet
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 왼쪽은 작은 회계 사무소, 오른쪽은 주방용품 가게. 둘 다 같은 높이의 상승 그래프 깃발을 달고 있음. 왼쪽 문으로는 손님이 계속 들어오고, 오른쪽 가게 위 광고판 전원 플러그가 뽑혀 있고 가게 앞이 한산함. 실제 브랜드 로고 사용 금지.

cards.title: You can buy one of them. What do you check first?
body: Both businesses cost the same, grew 40% last year and earn the same profit. You have time to dig into one question before you decide.

options.text: Which one sells into the bigger market
options.feedback: A bigger market gives more room to grow. But it says nothing about how each business actually reaches its customers.

options.text: Where new customers come from, and what happens if marketing spend stops
options.feedback: This tells you whether the growth belongs to the business or is bought fresh each month. The next card shows why it matters.

options.text: Which one spends less on marketing
options.feedback: Low spend can mean strong word of mouth, or a business that simply hasn't tried to grow. The amount spent tells you less than where customers come from.

cards.title: Three months without ads.
body: The bookkeeping firm won most clients through referrals from existing clients. The shop won most customers through online ads.
When the ads paused, the shop's flow of new customers fell by about three-quarters. The firm's barely moved.

Kitchenware shop: new customers vs normal

cards.title: Paid vs organic growth
body: **Paid growth** brings customers because you pay for each chance to reach them: ads, paid listings, sales commissions. **Organic growth** brings customers without a payment per customer: referrals, word of mouth, repeat visits, people who find you on their own.

Paid growth works like a tap. Turn it on and customers flow. Turn it off and they stop. Organic growth works more like a spring. It is slow to start, but it keeps flowing from what you have already built.

image.label: A tap next to a natural spring
image.brief: 좌우 대비 일러스트. 왼쪽은 동전 투입구가 달린 수도꼭지에서 물(작은 사람 아이콘들)이 나오고 "Paid" 라벨. 오른쪽은 바위 틈에서 솟는 샘물이 점점 넓어지는 개울이 되고 "Organic" 라벨. 차분한 색감.

cards.title: Each kind of growth has its own shape.
body: Neither is better in every way. They trade different strengths.
list: **Paid:** fast, easy to switch on, easy to measure, grows with budget
**Paid:** the price is set by others, and rivals can buy the same customers
**Organic:** slow, hard to control, hard to speed up
**Organic:** keeps working when you stop spending, and rivals can't simply buy it
cards.callout: Paid buys speed. Organic builds something that stays.

cards.title: The best paid customers turn organic.
body: The shop's ads weren't a mistake. They took it from zero to thousands of customers far faster than referrals could.

The real question is what happens after the first sale. If a customer the shop paid for comes back on their own and tells two friends, that paid sale has started an organic stream. If they buy once and vanish, the shop must pay again for every sale, forever.
cards.softwareNote: Watch the share of new signups that arrive with no ad behind them: invites, direct visits, search for your name. If that share grows as you grow, paid users are feeding organic growth.

cards.title: Organic is not free.
body: Referrals cost good service, time and the owner's attention. Earned search results cost months of writing and fixing. That cost is real, just harder to see on an invoice.

Organic flows can also be fragile. A search engine or marketplace can change its rules and cut your traffic overnight. And organic growth can be too slow: a young business may run out of cash waiting for word of mouth to spread.

cards.title: Now it's a booking app for hair salons.
body: Your app lets salons take online bookings. About 70% of new salon signups come from paid social ads, and ad prices keep rising. What do you do next?

options.text: Double the ad budget to grab salons before rivals do
options.feedback: You'd grow fast, but at prices others set and rising. If ads stop working, growth stops with them.

options.text: Keep ads, add a free month for salons that refer another, and track the share of signups with no ad behind them
options.feedback: You keep the speed of paid while building a stream that doesn't need a new payment each time. Tracking shows whether it's working.

options.text: Cut all ads and rely on word of mouth
options.feedback: It removes the rising cost, but growth may stall before referrals pick up. Organic is slow to start.

cards.title: Paid growth is rented. Organic growth is built.
body: Judge growth by where it comes from, not just how fast it is. Use paid to move quickly, and make sure it feeds a stream that keeps flowing without it.
**Try it today:** list where your last 20 customers came from. Mark the ones who would still have come if you had spent nothing.
